page.layout: One printed page of running text in one column. Running head at the top. No marginal notes. Headings centred below the text. No page number. Catchword at the right below the last line.

main_text.p: dorem & verecundiam mentis, simplici habi-tu incessuque ostendant. Obscenitate etiá me-brorum & verborum sicut & operum penitus exercentur. Viduarum & virginum frequenta-tiones penitus fugiant. Contubernia extranea-rum fœminarum nullatenus appetant. Casti-moniam quoque non violati corporis perpe-tuo obseruare studeant, AUT CERTE UNIUS MATRIMONII VINCULO FOEDERENTUR. Senioribus quoque de-bitam prebeant obedientiam, neque ullius ia-stantiæ studio semetipsos attollant. Postremò, doctrinæ, lectionibus, psalmis, hymnis, canticis, exercitio iugiter incumbant. Tales enim debet esse, qui divinis cultibus sese emancipados stu-dent, scilicet ut dùm scientiæ operam dant, do-ctrinæ gratiam populis administrent.
main_text.head: CONTRA LUXUM Sacerdotum.
CAPUT XXV. Clericos secularia non debere tractare.
main_text.p: Item 21.q.3. Mollicijs.) Mollicijs & seculari-bus rebus laqueisque obligari non debent, qui diuinis rebus & spiritualibus occupati sunt,

page.notes: The running head is printed as "SENTENTIAE DE*"; the trailing mark may be an ornament or a printer's sign. A small mark stands in the left margin near the middle of the page; it is not a note. The long s is written as a plain s throughout, as instructed, and the ligatures ct, st and st are read as their letters. The first paragraph is continued from the previous page. The catchword "nec" is printed at the lower right.
